title: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Integrated Investment Allowance discontinuance
sections.summary: MOF announced at Budget 2022 that the Integrated Investment Allowance scheme would be discontinued after 31 December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) had announced at Budget 2022 the discontinuance of the Integrated Investment Allowance (IIA) scheme after 31 December 2022.

sections.label: AFL scheme extension
sections.summary: Clause 7 will extend the AFL scheme to 31 December 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: First, clause 7 will extend the AFL scheme to 31 December 2028.

sections.label: ARI scheme amendments
sections.summary: Clauses 2, 10 and 12 extend the scheme by five years to 31 December 2028 and shift the ARI scheme to an activity-based approach from 1 April 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The legislative amendments in clauses 2, 10 and 12 will extend the scheme by five years to 31 December 2028 and enhance the administration of the ARI scheme by shifting from an agreement-based approach to an activity-based approach from 1 April 2023.

sections.label: PC and DEI extension
sections.summary: The Pioneer Certificate scheme and the Development and Expansion Incentive scheme will be extended by five years to 31 December 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Pioneer Certificate (PC) scheme and the Development and Expansion Incentive (DEI) scheme will be extended by five years to 31 December 2028.

sections.label: Singapore corporate ecosystem statistics
sections.summary: Singapore has close to 40,000 international companies contributing about 30% of employment and 56% to value added, with FDI inflow of $195 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore is home to a vibrant and diversified corporate ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are close to 40,000 international companies in Singapore, contributing about 30% of employment and 56% to value added over the past few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Foreign direct investment inflow into Singapore reached $195 billion in 2022, reflecting robust growth year-on-year.

sections.label: New Approved Activities scheme
sections.summary: The latest amendment to the Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) Bill introduces a new Approved Activities scheme in place of the ARI scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): The latest amendment to the Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) Bill seeks to enhance the existing incentives scheme by introducing a new Approved Activities scheme in place of the ARI scheme.

sections.label: Tax incentives and BEPS 2.0
sections.summary: Tax incentives must keep pace with national goals and business changes, but BEPS 2.0 guidelines challenge their effectiveness for large multinational enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It ensures that our tax incentives stay in step with both national goals and the changing landscapes of business and investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, it is crucial to be cognisant of broader international trends, like the forthcoming Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 guidelines, which pose a challenge to the effectiveness of Singapore's tax incentives, particularly for multinational enterprises with a global turnover of at least €750 million.

sections.label: Strategy for multinational enterprise innovation
sections.summary: The strategy keeps Singapore a top innovation destination, benefiting SMEs through international ties, business opportunities and technological partnerships, preserving competitiveness for sustainable development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Such a strategy ensures Singapore remains a top-tier destination for innovation among multinational enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These reforms not only appeal to MNCs but also generate a ripple effect that benefits small and medium-sized enterprises by enhancing their international ties, increasing business opportunities and fostering technological partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For a small, open economy like ours, these initiatives are critical by preserving our competitive edge and ensuring a favourable climate for sustainable economic development and the success of businesses of all scales.

sections.label: Approved royalty initiative scheme clauses
sections.summary: Clauses 10 to 12 amend sections 37 and 39 and introduce section 40, covering a new approved royalty initiative scheme with tax benefits for royalties, fees and R&D contributions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 10 through 12 make amendments to sections 37 and 39 of the original Act and also introduce a new section 40.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These all deal with a new approved royalty initiative or ARI scheme which spells out tax benefits for royalties as well as technical assistance fees or contributions to R&D costs.

sections.label: Concerns over ARI non-resident exemptions
sections.summary: The new ARI's differences from other incentives and its apparent tax exemptions for non-resident persons raise concern it could help companies skirt BEPS 2.0 obligations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Relatedly, how does the new ARI differ from the pioneer industry, pioneer service and development and expansion incentives that also appear to fall under the Economic Expansion Incentives Act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And, finally, my third and perhaps greatest concern has to do with the risk that the expanded scope of the new ARI seems to now offer tax exemptions to non-resident persons, as opposed to being limited to the current treatment where royalties qualify for tax concessions only if they are earned in Singapore by either residents or permanent establishments here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 40(b), for instance, states that and, I quote, "relevant royalties, fees or contributions are payable to a non-resident person during the period of approval for that activity." If this is true, I am concerned that the provision may inadvertently become a means for international companies to use the R&D tax credits as a means of skirting their BEPS 2.0 minimum tax obligations, with very little direct benefits to Singapore.

sections.label: Ireland GNI and GDP
sections.summary: Accounting for depreciation of IP reviews, gross national income is only a little more than half of official gross domestic product in Ireland.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, accounting for depreciation of IP reviews, by one calculation, gross national income (GNI) is only a little more than half of official gross domestic product (GDP) in Ireland.

sections.label: Revenue impact of international tax agreement
sections.summary: The agreement is progressing on Pillar 1 amounts A and B and Pillar 2 subject to tax rule, and MOF previously said Pillar 1 will result in a loss of revenue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As this House is well aware, the agreement continues to grind inexorably forward, most recently making significant progress on negotiation pertaining to amounts A and B of Pillar 1 and subject to tax rule of Pillar 2.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry, therefore, share with this House whether it has made progress in projections of the potential revenue impact should the agreement proceed as planned?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MOF had previously explained, and I quote, that "Pillar 1 will result in a loss of revenue".

sections.label: Singapore non-tax competitiveness post-BEPS
sections.summary: The Ministry said Singapore will need to strengthen non-tax factors to stay competitive in a post-BEPS world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Ministry has indicated that Singapore will need to strengthen non-tax factors to stay competitive in a post-BEPS world.

sections.label: Pillar 2 and tax incentives
sections.summary: Mark Lee noted Pillar 2 could reduce the effectiveness of certain tax incentives, as multinationals with revenues of at least €750 million must bear a 15% minimum effective tax rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Mr Mark Lee also correctly noted that the implementation of Pillar 2 of BEPS 2.0 could reduce the effectiveness of certain tax incentives since multinational enterprises with consolidated annual revenues of at least €750 million would have to bear a minimum effective tax rate (METR) of 15%, wherever they operate.

sections.label: Pillar 2 scope and withholding taxes
sections.summary: Multinationals below the €750 million revenue threshold are outside Pillar 2 and keep concessionary tax rate incentives, and the 15% METR does not apply to withholding taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, multinationals under the revenue threshold of €750 million are not in the scope of Pillar 2, as Members known, and will thus continue to benefit from concessionary tax rate incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Second, the METR of 15% under Pillar 2 does not apply to withholding taxes, which the AFL and ARI schemes seek to reduce.
